Surbooking
Turn your phoneSurbooking is played upright.
EDEN

Detailed rules
Story
Radiation has made the planet uninhabitable. Unwanted side effect: some irradiated animals clone themselves, and those are the ones you meet in the last sections. The ark The Last Seat carries two healthy animals per species and a single human seat. Its AI, EDEN, has thawed out 32 candidates for that seat: welcome to Surbooking. Each floor is a section of the ark, from Quarantine to the Menagerie, then the arena, just below the cockpit. Rejects go back to cryosleep. The rest, EDEN will tell the last passenger.
EDEN
She speaks over the ark's loudspeakers: her lines appear as subtitles, then fade; the history stays in the combat log. The speaker button, top right, mutes or unmutes her voice; she speaks by default, and your choice is remembered.
Rooms
After each combat you win, a single room, drawn at random: shop, chest or event (?). Some events are tempting offers paid for in HP or tickets: laboratory, black market, cracked tank, nurse, training room, complaints desk (swap a white for a white of your main family, 10 tickets), EDEN's bet (stake 10 tickets: EDEN pays you 30 if you win the next combat within her turn target) and decontamination shower (incinerate a basic card, 4 HP). One time in three, behind the (?) door, it’s an EDEN appointment: a short scene, two or three choices, each showing what it costs and what it gives; the same scene never comes back within a run.
Tickets
10 per combat won, plus 5 if you win within the turn target (shown top right during combat), plus 5 if you lose no HP. They don't count toward the score.
Basic cards
8 cards given by your class: 4 attacks and 4 defenses (Candidate: 4 Bare Fists for 4 damage and 4 Dodges for 4 Block). You own them from the start; they can't be drafted, don't fuse, count toward no family and aren't low blows.
Turbulence
Difficulty levels, solo only (live play and the daily session stay at base level). Winning the final unlocks level 1, then each win at your highest level unlocks the next, up to 20. You pick the level on the class screen; each one adds its constraint to the previous ones (1: monsters +10% HP; 2: floor bosses +15% HP; 3: candidates across from you +10% HP; 4: healing −25%; 5: monsters +10% damage; 6: monsters +1 Strength at the start of combat; 7: one fewer card on turn one; 8: candidates across from you +1 Strength; 9: each floor starts at 95% HP; 10: final opponent +15% HP; 11: monsters start combat with Block, 6 in quarantine and 2 more per floor; 12: half as many tickets per win; 13: shop +50%; 14: monsters another +15% damage; 15: 1 less energy on turn one against monsters; 16: monsters another +20% HP; 17: the floor boss gains 1 Strength every two turns, unless frozen; 18: each floor starts at 85% HP; 19: candidates across from you another +20% HP and +1 Strength; 20: final opponent another +20% HP and 2 Strength) and earns 10% more wardrobe points.
Classes
Before the first draft, you choose your former job. It sets your basic cards, your max HP (proportionally, on every floor and in the final) and a playstyle: an upside and a downside of similar size, useful with any deck. No class gets a bonus against a type of opponent, or for a family or card type: the draft stays open. Candidate: the baseline, 103% HP, Bare Fist (4 damage) and Dodge (4 Block), no talent and no drawback. Veterinarian (the healer): Tranquilizer Dart (4 damage) and First Aid (3 Block, heal 1 HP); Healer: at the start of each of your turns, if you have lost HP, you recover 1 in Quarantine, 2 on later floors (4 in the final); Fragile: max HP −2%. Ark Mechanic (the tempo): Wrench (3 damage, 1 Block) and Riveted Plate (4 Block, carries over to next turn); Hot Start: 1 extra energy on the first turn of each combat; Overheat: 1 less energy on the second turn; max HP +3%. Cargo Stowaway (the draft snoop): Sucker Punch (1 damage, draw 1 card) and Take Cover (0 energy, 1 Block); Snoop: once per draft, from Quarantine on, take 2 cards from the same pack (not at pick 4 or pick 8; the pack you pass has one card fewer); Groggy: 1 fewer card on the first turn of each combat. Standby Passenger (the gamble): Suitcase Swing (4 damage) and Life Vest (4 Block); Upgrade: at the start of each of your turns, a random card in your hand costs 1 less; Excess Baggage: another costs 1 more, and max HP −7%. Maintenance Android (stored energy): Discharge (4 damage) and Standby Mode (4 Block), max HP +4%; Battery: 1 unspent energy is kept for the next turn; Bodywork: healing (cards and rooms) restores a quarter less HP. The other candidates at the table also have a class, drawn at random: they play its basic cards, with its HP modifier and its duel effects (recovery, energy, draw; Snoop, which only matters in the draft, is for the player alone). PvP ghosts keep their player's class.
Draft
4 booster packs of 12 cards: one headliner (green 1 time in 4, otherwise white) and 11 whites in Quarantine (on later floors, two headliners and 10 filler cards). Take a card, pass the rest to the left: 12 picks. At picks 5 and 9, your first pack comes back around: that's the wheel.
Keep 8
After the 12th pick, you keep 8 of your cards (EDEN preselects 8; change whatever you like); the other 4 go to the incinerator. Fusions wait for this choice: a kept pair fuses, a discarded pair doesn't. Every card you own goes into your deck: it grows by 8 cards each floor.
Fusion
Automatic: as soon as you own 2 identical cards, they fuse, chaining if needed. 2 identical whites make the green of their line, 2 identical greens make the blue, 2 identical blues make the purple, whether the cards come from the draft (during the draft, as soon as you pick), a chest, the shop or an event. Your deck loses a card with each fusion, but never any family points: the fused card keeps the points of both its cards. 2 whites (2 points) make a green (2 points); 2 greens (4 points) make a blue worth 4 points instead of 3; 2 blues make a purple worth 6, 7 or 8 points (instead of 4) depending on the blues fused. These points are written on the card, next to its family, and leave with it if it leaves the deck. So a fusion always pays off. Basic cards, purples, oranges and reds don't fuse. The other candidates fuse their pairs the same way.
Families
Every card belongs to a family (Instinct, Armor, Scrounge, Mutation, Cryo, Multiplication, Faith, Sacrifice). A card's “Combo” line tells you what it combines with.
Specialization
White 1 point, green 2, blue 3, purple 4 (in the final: orange 5, red 6); a fused card keeps the points of both its cards (see Fusion). Each family has three tiers, at 4, 8 and 16 points, which stack: the first is a small bonus, the third changes how you play. A fourth, at 36 points, is for the most stubborn: it takes a deck almost entirely from one family, and is mostly reached in the final. Only your two strongest families are active (main and secondary); a third family stays dormant until it overtakes them. Rivals specialize too: your boss uses it against you.
Low blows
In the Greenhouse and the Menagerie, a few green cards with no family slip into the booster packs: Elbow Jab, Trip, False Testimony, Bribe. Weak against a monster, they are strong against a candidate, in duels and in the final. They count toward no family. The other candidates draft them too, and play them against you. Several low blows grow stronger, outside the two-family limit: at 2, Sneaky (a low blow is in your hand on the first turn of each duel and of the final); at 3, Devious (your first low blow each turn costs nothing against a candidate); at 5, Scoundrel (their effect is doubled against a candidate).
Orange and red
Two rarities found only in the final: orange is legendary, red is mythic. One of each per family. They don't fuse, and count for 5 and 6 family points toward tiers: a single one can unlock a tier right before the duel.
Final boss
The deck always comes from the other finalist, but the final has four faces, drawn at random and announced before the final draft. The candidate (4 times in 10): the winner of the other duel, as is. The mutated candidate (1 time in 4): at the end of each of their turns, their most expensive card duplicates into their hand; Frozen, they don't proliferate. The escaped monster (1 time in 4): the Mother, with the other finalist's deck and animal cards; she spawns an offspring every two turns, her offspring follow her into cryo, but each offspring killed sends her into a fury. EDEN (1 time in 10): she disqualifies the other finalist, keeps their deck and replaces its basic cards with protocols that drain your energy, make you discard or invent a rule mid-combat (Austerity, Tax, Quota, Flat Rate), from turn one.
Final
After the last floor, two candidates remain: you, and the winner of the other duel at your table. First, a head-to-head draft: each of you opens a 4-card pack (your red, an orange, a purple and a blue, from four different families), takes a card and passes the rest to the other, up to 4 picks each. Your opponent is announced before this draft: whatever you leave them, they will play. Then a single duel, with HP restored. For now the opponent is a bot playing the other finalist's deck, with 534 HP against your 336 (for a Candidate; both numbers follow the class modifier) to make up for playing worse than a human. The winner takes the last seat; the loser finishes second.
Bonus act
After a final won solo (not live, not in the daily session), EDEN offers to send you down to the engine room, if you want: a lightning draft (12 blue and purple cards and one orange; you keep 3), then a single duel, at full HP, in the reactor leak (at the start of each of your turns, +1 Radiation for you and for him), against the former co-pilot, who plays the deck of a real recorded final winner (or, failing that, your final opponent’s). Win it and the ship takes off; losing doesn’t cost you your seat. The act gives no extra wardrobe points and isn’t counted in the statistics.
Seed
Every run has its seed, shown on the end screen: the same seed gives the same booster packs and the same encounters. “Replay this seed”, or in Collection, “Replay a seed”.
Jack-of-all-trades
With 6 families at 4 points or more, active or dormant, a third family becomes active (the strongest after your top two), and your basic cards get +2 (Bare Fists 6 damage, Dodges 6 Block; same for the other classes' basic cards). At 7 families, a fourth family becomes active. It's the catch-up for those who spread themselves thin: rare by chance, reachable in the Greenhouse if you aim for it, common in the Menagerie for anyone drafting without a plan. The other candidates get it too.
Turn
3 energy and 5 cards drawn. Your hand is discarded at end of turn (except “on ice” cards and your stack of Rabbits).
Block
Absorbs damage. Expires at the start of your turn, except with Crate Barricade or Containment Airlock (or half of it with Shell).
Charge
Armor cards that Charge (Shoulder Bash, Armored Charge, Battering Ram, Bow Ram…) deal damage equal to your Block, with no cap, then you lose half of it. The timing is yours: charging early leaves you exposed; waiting hits harder.
Strength
Each attack deals X more damage, until the end of combat.
On instinct
Instinct's claws are stronger when they are the first card you play in the turn: Claw Swipe, Claw Flurry and Wolverine Frenzy land one more hit. Only one card per turn benefits: opening with a Strength card or a Dodge gives it up.
Last scrap
Scrounge's Trays, Carts, Banquet and Buffet hit twice when they are the last card in your hand. Drawing becomes a gamble: every card drawn is one more card to empty.
Radiation
The target (monster or candidate: the moths give you some) loses X HP at the start of its turn, ignoring Block, then X drops by 1 (except with the Mutant specialization). In a duel, against a candidate, X is halved every turn (it only loses a third with Mutant, and nothing with Exposed Reactor). Accelerated Mutation doubles it, Runaway Mutation quadruples it. Clones are born with the Radiation of whoever spawned them.
Reaction
Culture Drop and Petri Dish make their target react: it immediately takes half its Radiation, which stays whole. Play them after your other Radiation cards.
Freeze
Freeze X: the first hit of each of your attacks against the target deals X more damage. Freeze adds up from card to card; at the end of the target's turn, half of it remains (with Deep Freeze, the 8-point Cryo tier, it no longer melts). It takes nothing from the target: no energy, no damage. A “Freeze 3, then 2 damage” card benefits from its own Freeze: it deals 5. As long as it has Freeze, a monster is Frozen: it can't fly into a fury, heal or clone.
Shattering Freeze
Icebreaker and Pod Shard remove all Freeze from their target (half with Deep Freeze) and deal extra damage for each Freeze shattered. Play them last: shattered Freeze no longer helps your next attacks.
On ice
An “on ice” card you don't play stays in your hand next turn, and gains its bonus every turn you keep it (you still draw 5 cards). Thaw (Cryo Pod): cards already kept cost 0 this turn.
Encounters
Each floor: the duel, right after the draft, then a monster fight, then the floor boss, with a room between fights. The monster fight changes from run to run (shown in the floor's encounter list): in Quarantine, the capybaras (every third turn, Hector sits on you: 7 damage, watch the intents), cargo rats or cockroaches that get back up once (7 HP) unless Frozen or irradiated; in the Stable, guard geese, greedy pigs that eat if they haven't been hit since their last turn (+8 HP, +1 Strength, unless Frozen) or an irradiated brood of four chicks that grow into hens after three turns (unless Frozen); in the Greenhouse, moths, cactus toads or puffballs that burst when sent to cryo (4 Radiation on you, unless Frozen); in the Menagerie, mutant rabbits or Schrödinger's cat, in its box every other turn, where your hits deal only half (Frozen, it is observed and takes everything).
Floors
At each table, right after the draft, two duels: you against the candidate sitting across from you, and the other two against each other (simulated). Across the table, nobody has the edge: each of you picks before the other in two packs out of four. Losers are eliminated. Then you must survive the floor up to its boss, with the HP left after the duel. After that, HP goes back to max, the deck is kept, and a new draft is played at a new table.
Cloning
A mutant ewe clones herself every few end-of-turns (at half her HP), three ewes at most. Frozen, she doesn't clone. A clone is born with its mother's Radiation: irradiate her before she clones. In the Menagerie, both rabbits clone every two turns (at 40% of their HP, six rabbits at most), and when one of the two original rabbits goes into cryo, the other clones at once, unless Frozen.
The Mother
Boss of the Menagerie. At the end of each turn she spawns a 17 HP offspring on her own, four at most, unless she is Frozen. When she goes into cryo, her offspring follow her: you can take her down and ignore them.
Thorns
Each hit you land on a cactus toad deals its thorns to you as damage. Multi-hit attacks suffer for it.
Unstable
In the Greenhouse, when one member of a couple goes into cryo, the other mutates instead of flying into a fury: +10 HP and a stronger effect. Frozen, it doesn't mutate.
Duel
The first encounter of each floor, right after the draft, against the candidate sitting across from you, with the cards they just drafted, their basic cards and their deck from earlier floors. They arrive at full HP, like you. Their intents are hidden. You go first, with 4 cards and 2 energy on turn one; they get 4 cards on their first turn (the same rule as live play, so going first doesn't decide the duel). After the 15th turn, whoever has lost the larger share of their max HP loses. Winning a duel restores 25% of your max HP.
Floor boss
The last encounter of each floor: a lone monster with visible intents. Quarantine: the scapegoat, which chews up your most expensive card (discarded at the start of your turn), or Gaston the bull, who telegraphs his charge. Stable: Dolly, the irradiated ewe who clones herself, or the cleaning unit RX-7. Greenhouse: the giant flytrap, whose vines drain 1 energy from you and which digests to heal (blocked by Radiation or Freeze), or Teddy the mutant bear, or the Serpent, who offers you an apple. Menagerie: the Mother, the Chimera, or the Tank Leviathan, which swallows you. You must beat it to move up.
Rabbits
Multiplication keeps its Rabbits in a single card, “Rabbits ×N”, in your hand. Some cards create them, others double or triple them. Played as is (0 energy), each Rabbit lands its own hit for 3 damage (5 with Long Teeth), then the stack is spent. Some cards release them differently: in a single hit, stronger per Rabbit. If you don't play it, the stack stays in your hand next turn (you still draw 5 cards): release now, or hold to multiply. It never exceeds 20 Rabbits.
Offering
Faith cards that “offer a card” have you choose another card in your hand: it is removed from combat and gives you Fervor according to its rarity (basic card 4, white 6, green 8, blue 10, purple 12, orange 14, red 16; a stack of Rabbits: 3 per Rabbit). A card you couldn't have paid for makes a fine offering.
Fervor
It is added to the first hit of your next attack, then drops back to zero. It is not lost from one turn to the next.
Act of Faith
The top card of your draw pile is played for free, sight unseen, on the same target. If it can't be played, it is discarded. An Offering played this way picks the card it offers by itself.
Sacrifice
Some cards cost a percentage of your max HP: the number of HP is written on the card in your hand. They cannot kill you: you cannot play them without enough HP. Blood Spilled rises by the percentage your cards take from you (a 5% card raises it by 5, on every floor); some cards strike or protect you according to it, and each HP healed lowers it by 1. Raw (at half your HP or less) and at death's door (at a quarter or less), some cards are stronger.
Weak
Deals 25% less damage.
Vulnerable
Takes 50% more damage.
Fury
When one member of a couple goes into cryo, the other gains damage. Geese attack immediately.
Depressurization
15 turns max per combat. After that, your application is rejected.
Score
Eliminates no one: added up over the floors you clear, it gives your run points, which will buy skins. 100 × HP left / max HP, plus 10 per achievement, plus 5 per turn ahead of the floor's target, the sum of the targets of its three fights (25 max).
Skin shop
At the end of a run (elimination, final, or a new draft started after clearing a floor), its run points go to EDEN’s wardrobe. There you open crates (cargo, 200 points; captain’s, 450 points, rare and up): each one gives a random skin you don’t have yet, for cards (frames, family tints, backs) or for your character (hair, leaf, outfit, accessory). The odds are shown. Purely cosmetic: no skin changes the game.
Outfit
From 4 points in a family, your main specialization dresses you in a costume (the penguin for Cryo, the locker breastplate for Armor…) and your secondary one puts a prop in your hand; with Jack-of-all-trades, the third fills the other hand. The same items for every class. At tier 16, the item glows. Dormant families aren't worn.
